clue.text: Obtained information from returning journalist, brusque little man

indicators.note: returning means the word for journalist is read backwards here

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist
brusque means curt or brief
Ed is a short form of Edward, a man's name made little

explanation.surface: Someone extracted a story from a curt, small reporter heading back to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ED into DE; the second ED is a pet name for Edward, the little man.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them about a completed mission, so the past tense means having obtained information from them.

clue.text: Duke and stranger ramble

parts.note: stranger means more odd

explanation.surface: A nobleman and an outsider go walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodder is to move or talk in a shaky, aimless way, like wandering.

clue.text: Sort of criminal, large with a dim appearance

parts.note: large means big
a mist gives things a dim, hazy look

explanation.surface: A hulking crook with a shadowy look.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already married is a crime, so one who does it is an offender.

clue.text: Favoured having diplomacy undiminished

parts.note: being in means being in favour
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Someone in favour keeps tactfulness whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left whole and unharmed is untouched, with nothing taken away.

clue.text: Earlier tool used for shaping

explanation.surface: An earlier shaping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means previous, and also a template or mould on which things are shaped.

clue.text: Politician almost a devil — Conservative deserter

indicators.note: almost means the word for a devil stops one letter short

parts.note: a demon is a devil
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: A nearly diabolical politician who abandoned the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US left-of-centre party is a politician.

clue.text: Electronic device rendering lyric written in 2000

indicators.note: written in means the poem is placed inside the number's letters

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is a thousand, so two thousand is MM
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A gadget that produced a song in the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering' is only a link; the number 2000 is written as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is the box that lets a computer send data over phone or cable lines, an electronic gadget.

clue.text: Messages from singer burl's daughter?

parts.note: an unmarried daughter would be addressed as Miss
Burl Ives was an American folk singer

explanation.surface: Letters sent by a famous singer's girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Burl Ives was an American folk singer; his unmarried daughter would be Miss Ives.
explanation.definitionFit: A missive is a letter or written message.

clue.text: Party male in old mask

parts.note: a do is a party
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man at a party wearing an antique mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small eye mask worn at a masquerade.

clue.text: Maiden and I row, being discontented folk

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over
a row is a series or line

explanation.surface: A girl and I argue, ending up unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but means a line, SERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a misery is a gloomy, complaining person, so the plural means grumblers.

clue.text: Something bright in the night sky worries sailor

definitions.text: Something bright in the night sky

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or harass them persistently
TAR is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A brilliant celestial body troubles a seaman on night watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star seen at night, is nicknamed after the hound of Orion.

clue.text: In a time of darkness some light nonsense?

definitions.text: In a time of darkness some light

explanation.surface: Some light at night, or so the clue claims, may be rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Light reflected from our satellite shines at night, and the same word is slang for foolish talk.

clue.text: Violent rioters or just one noisy reveller?

indicators.note: violent suggests the rioters are thrown into disorder, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is this a gang of violent rioters, or merely a single loud partygoer?
explanation.walkthrough: The plural rioters becomes the single reveller; 'or just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the archaic word means a boisterous merrymaker, a carouser.

clue.text: Food eaten by Esther, a violinist

indicators.note: eaten by means the food sits swallowed inside the words Esther, a violinist

explanation.surface: A violinist called Esther has a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pasta parcels filled with meat or cheese are an Italian dish.

clue.text: Three figures to define a single figure?

definitions.text: Three figures to define a single figure?

parts.words: Three figures to define a single figure?
parts.note: the first figures are numbers, the second is a body shape: bust, waist and hip measurements

explanation.surface: Three numbers sum up one person's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements, the numbers describing her shape.

clue.text: One American soldier left in vehicle, tense and watchful

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a van is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one
GI is a US soldier
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A lone US soldier sits nervously alert in a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Being vigilant means keeping careful watch for danger.

clue.text: Much less stock is stored in shelter

indicators.note: is stored in means the stock word is put inside the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
in card games the talon is the stock, the pile left after dealing

explanation.surface: Supplies are kept in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: TALON is a card-game term for the undealt pile, the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning not to mention, used as in 'he cannot walk, much less run'.

clue.text: The end for united, lacking caution in the middle — badly beaten

indicators.note: in the middle means the rash word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
rash means reckless, lacking caution

indicators.note: end for points to the last letter of the word united

explanation.surface: A football report: United played recklessly at the back and were hammered.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus D, the end of 'united', has RASH placed 'in the middle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrashed is to be beaten heavily, in a fight or a match.

clue.text: Lonely oldie sat looking out of sorts

indicators.note: out of sorts means disordered, so the letters of oldie sat are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old person sat about looking unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling cut off from others, with no company, is being solitary.

clue.text: Thinner relation settling in Germany

indicators.note: settling in means the relative goes inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: an aunt is a family relation

explanation.surface: A relative who moved to Germany has grown leaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaunt means lean and haggard, so the comparative means more emaciated.

clue.text: Church interior hides ragamuffin

indicators.note: hides means the answer is concealed within the words Church interior

explanation.surface: A street child is sheltering inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruffy, mischievous child is a street kid.

clue.text: Weed in flower finally, a growth endlessly out of control

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word flower
out of control suggests letters running wild, so they are rearranged
endlessly means the word growth loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A weed in a flower bed has spread unchecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims growth to GROWT, which 'out of control' rearranges to GWORT; before it come R from 'flower finally' and A.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered plant, poisonous to livestock, is treated as a troublesome weed in Britain.

clue.text: Pony trekking maybe in old part of Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Taking ponies out in the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire, an English county, was long divided into three administrative regions, North, East and West, under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pony trekking is an example of horseback travel, and the word also names each historic third of Yorkshire.

clue.text: Mass starts to get really animated — marvellous musical experience

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.words: get really animated — marvellous musical experience

explanation.surface: A huge crowd gets excited at a wonderful concert.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric unit of weight is a measure of mass.

clue.text: Sort of sandwich, savoury with egg in

indicators.note: in means the egg shape goes inside the savoury word

parts.note: savoury food is tasty
O looks like an egg in shape

explanation.surface: A tasty sandwich with egg filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sandwich is called by this word, a variant of toastie.

clue.text: Old Celia's moving around in a restricted area

indicators.note: moving around means the letters of Old Celia's shift into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly woman named Celia moves about within a confined space.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Celia's is used as a letter in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confined to one particular spot, such as a pain, is described with this word.

clue.text: It's mean to upset people in an institution

indicators.note: to upset means to knock over, so the letters of It's mean are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone declares that causing distress is unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners or patients housed in a jail or hospital are its residents.

clue.text: Colour no good in item of clothing

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: a tie is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A shade judged poor in a piece of attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a tint.

clue.text: One of the times when letters are collected?

definitions.text: One of the times when letters are collected?

parts.words: One of the times when letters are collected?
parts.note: the letters are not post but initials such as BA, collected at a graduation ceremony

explanation.surface: A postbox notice lists the collection times.
explanation.definitionFit: On graduation day students receive their qualifications, the letters after their name.
